structure.title: Hopes placed in others
structure.text: Early books introduce ambitions for marriage, scholarship, and medicine, alongside the social assumptions supporting them.

structure.title: A web of consequences
structure.text: The eight books interweave households and professions, showing how a choice alters lives beyond the chooser's knowledge.

people.name: Dorothea Brooke
people.text: An earnest, high-minded young woman in a provincial town who longs to do something great with her life and has no obvious way to do it.

people.name: Lydgate
people.text: A gifted young doctor new to Middlemarch, full of plans to reform medicine, who underestimates how much the town will shape him.

people.name: Casaubon
people.text: An older clergyman and scholar who has spent decades on a grand work of learning, and whom Dorothea mistakes for a great mind.

context.title: A town as a network
context.text: Reputation, credit, marriage, and professional opportunity pass through shared relationships. No major character controls the whole web.
context.takeaway: Follow consequences beyond the central couple.

context.title: Reform and profession
context.text: Political and medical change challenge established habits. New ideas still need money, cooperation, and trust to become effective.

notice.text: Notice the narrator correcting a quick judgment.
notice.why: Another person's circumstances can change the meaning of an action.
Ambition is reshaped through small practical decisions.

opening: Dorothea wants a life devoted to something larger than herself and thinks marriage to a learned man will provide it. Lydgate arrives in town intending to transform medicine, confident that ordinary provincial compromises will not catch him. Both have admirable ambitions and incomplete knowledge of the people they need. George Eliot follows their hopes into marriages, debts, gossip, and daily negotiations, giving the supporting characters lives substantial enough to overturn a simple explanation of why someone else's future has gone wrong.
